No other disease, control, diagram or quality problem is present.

plate_findings.evidence: Diffuse erythematous scaly rash on the face (sun-exposed site)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the face showing a diffuse erythematous scaly rash in a sun-exposed distribution, consistent with pellagrous dermatitis in a patient whose article diagnosis is pellagra (the 3 Ds: dermatitis, diarrhea, altered mental status). The initial impression of seborrheic dermatitis was a misdiagnosis later attributed to pellagra. B: Clinical photograph of both lower extremities showing hyperpigmented, scaly, erythematous rash on extensor surfaces, a classic distribution of pellagrous dermatitis in a patient diagnosed with pellagra. C: Clinical photograph of the lower extremity/foot showing scaly, hyperpigmented erythematous rash consistent with pellagrous dermatitis in a patient diagnosed with pellagra.

in_text_mentions: On day 10 of hospitalization, the patient exhibited a rash on his face, scalp, and extremities (Figure 1). This was thought to be due to seborrheic dermatitis. His oral mucosa and tongue examination were normal without any sign of stomatitis or glossitis. On day 12, the patient developed fever, worsening diarrhea, and shock, prompting a transfer to the ICU. In the ICU, vasopressors and hydrocortisone were initiated due to suspected adrenal insufficiency. Further laboratory results showed central adrenal insufficiency with low levels of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and cortisol (Table 1).
